audit_status.review_note: First-pass draft reviewed for Israelite multiplication, Pharaoh's oppression, forced labor, midwives' resistance, and birth politics.

familiar.text: And all the souls that came out of the loins of Jacob were seventy souls: for Joseph was in Egypt already.

modern.text: The descendants of Jacob numbered seventy in all, including Joseph, who was already in Egypt.

original.text: וַֽיְהִ֗י כָּל נֶ֛פֶשׁ יֹצְאֵ֥י יֶֽרֶךְ יַעֲקֹ֖ב שִׁבְעִ֣ים נָ֑פֶשׁ וְיוֹסֵ֖ף הָיָ֥ה בְמִצְרָֽיִם

verses.restored: And Joseph died, and all his brothers, and all that generation.

familiar.text: And Joseph died, and all his brethren, and all that generation.

modern.text: Now Joseph and all his brothers and all that generation died,

original.text: וַיָּ֤מָת יוֹסֵף֙ וְכָל אֶחָ֔יו וְכֹ֖ל הַדּ֥וֹר הַהֽוּא

verses.restored: But the children of Israel were fruitful, swarmed, multiplied, and became exceedingly mighty; and the land was filled with them.

familiar.text: And the children of Israel were fruitful, and increased abundantly, and multiplied, and waxed exceeding mighty; and the land was filled with them.

modern.text: but the Israelites were fruitful and increased rapidly; they multiplied and became exceedingly numerous, so that the land was filled with them. Oppression by a New King (Acts 7:15–19)

original.text: וּבְנֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֗ל פָּר֧וּ וַֽיִּשְׁרְצ֛וּ וַיִּרְבּ֥וּ וַיַּֽעַצְמ֖וּ בִּמְאֹ֣ד מְאֹ֑ד וַתִּמָּלֵ֥א הָאָ֖רֶץ אֹתָֽם

verses.restored: And a new king arose over Egypt who did not know Joseph.

familiar.text: Now there arose up a new king over Egypt, which knew not Joseph.

modern.text: Then a new king, who did not know Joseph, came to power in Egypt.

original.text: וַיָּ֥קָם מֶֽלֶךְ חָדָ֖שׁ עַל מִצְרָ֑יִם אֲשֶׁ֥ר לֹֽא יָדַ֖ע אֶת יוֹסֵֽף

verses.restored: He said to his people, Look, the people of the children of Israel are more numerous and mighty than we.

familiar.text: And he said unto his people, Behold, the people of the children of Israel are more and mightier than we:

modern.text: “Look,” he said to his people, “the Israelites have become too numerous and too powerful for us.

original.text: וַיֹּ֖אמֶר אֶל עַמּ֑וֹ הִנֵּ֗ה עַ֚ם בְּנֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל רַ֥ב וְעָצ֖וּם מִמֶּֽנּוּ

verses.restored: Come, let us deal shrewdly with them, lest they multiply, and it happen that when war is called, they also join our enemies and fight against us and go up from the land.

familiar.text: Come on, let us deal wisely with them; lest they multiply, and it come to pass, that, when there falleth out any war, they join also unto our enemies, and fight against us, and so get them up out of the land.

modern.text: Come, let us deal shrewdly with them, or they will increase even more; and if a war breaks out, they may join our enemies, fight against us, and leave the country. ”

original.text: הָ֥בָה נִֽתְחַכְּמָ֖ה ל֑וֹ פֶּן יִרְבֶּ֗ה וְהָיָ֞ה כִּֽי תִקְרֶ֤אנָה מִלְחָמָה֙ וְנוֹסַ֤ף גַּם הוּא֙ עַל שֹׂ֣נְאֵ֔ינוּ וְנִלְחַם בָּ֖נוּ וְעָלָ֥ה מִן הָאָֽרֶץ

verses.restored: So they set over them forced-labor chiefs to afflict them with burdens; and they built storage cities for Pharaoh: Pithom and Raamses.

familiar.text: Therefore they did set over them taskmasters to afflict them with their burdens. And they built for Pharaoh treasure cities, Pithom and Raamses.

modern.text: So the Egyptians appointed taskmasters over the Israelites to oppress them with forced labor. As a result, they built Pithom and Rameses as store cities for Pharaoh.

original.text: וַיָּשִׂ֤ימוּ עָלָיו֙ שָׂרֵ֣י מִסִּ֔ים לְמַ֥עַן עַנֹּת֖וֹ בְּסִבְלֹתָ֑ם וַיִּ֜בֶן עָרֵ֤י מִסְכְּנוֹת֙ לְפַרְעֹ֔ה אֶת פִּתֹ֖ם וְאֶת רַעַמְסֵֽס

verses.restored: But the more they afflicted them, the more they multiplied and spread out; and they felt dread before the children of Israel.

familiar.text: But the more they afflicted them, the more they multiplied and grew. And they were grieved because of the children of Israel.

modern.text: But the more they were oppressed, the more they multiplied and flourished; so the Egyptians came to dread the Israelites.

original.text: וְכַאֲשֶׁר֙ יְעַנּ֣וּ אֹת֔וֹ כֵּ֥ן יִרְבֶּ֖ה וְכֵ֣ן יִפְרֹ֑ץ וַיָּקֻ֕צוּ מִפְּנֵ֖י בְּנֵ֥י יִשְׂרָאֵֽל

verses.restored: Egypt made the children of Israel serve with crushing labor.

familiar.text: And the Egyptians made the children of Israel to serve with rigour:

modern.text: They worked the Israelites ruthlessly

original.text: וַיַּעֲבִ֧דוּ מִצְרַ֛יִם אֶת בְּנֵ֥י יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל בְּפָֽרֶךְ

verses.restored: They made their lives bitter with hard service in mortar and brick and in every kind of service in the field; all their service with which they made them serve was with crushing force.

familiar.text: And they made their lives bitter with hard bondage, in morter, and in brick, and in all manner of service in the field: all their service, wherein they made them serve, was with rigour.

modern.text: and made their lives bitter with hard labor in brick and mortar, and with all kinds of work in the fields. Every service they imposed was harsh.

original.text: וַיְמָרְר֨וּ אֶת חַיֵּיהֶ֜ם בַּעֲבֹדָ֣ה קָשָׁ֗ה בְּחֹ֨מֶר֙ וּבִלְבֵנִ֔ים וּבְכָל עֲבֹדָ֖ה בַּשָּׂדֶ֑ה אֵ֚ת כָּל עֲבֹ֣דָתָ֔ם אֲשֶׁר עָבְד֥וּ בָהֶ֖ם בְּפָֽרֶךְ

verses.restored: The king of Egypt spoke to the Hebrew midwives, one whose name was Shiphrah and the second whose name was Puah,

familiar.text: And the king of Egypt spake to the Hebrew midwives, of which the name of the one was Shiphrah, and the name of the other Puah:

modern.text: Then the king of Egypt said to the Hebrew midwives, whose names were Shiphrah and Puah,

original.text: וַיֹּ֨אמֶר֙ מֶ֣לֶךְ מִצְרַ֔יִם לַֽמְיַלְּדֹ֖ת הָֽעִבְרִיֹּ֑ת אֲשֶׁ֨ר שֵׁ֤ם הָֽאַחַת֙ שִׁפְרָ֔ה וְשֵׁ֥ם הַשֵּׁנִ֖ית פּוּעָֽה

verses.restored: and he said, When you serve as midwives to the Hebrew women and see upon the birth-stools, if it is a son, put him to death; but if it is a daughter, she shall live.

familiar.text: And he said, When ye do the office of a midwife to the Hebrew women, and see them upon the stools; if it be a son, then ye shall kill him: but if it be a daughter, then she shall live.

modern.text: “When you help the Hebrew women give birth, observe them on the birthstools. If the child is a son, kill him; but if it is a daughter, let her live.”

original.text: וַיֹּ֗אמֶר בְּיַלֶּדְכֶן֙ אֶת הָֽעִבְרִיּ֔וֹת וּרְאִיתֶ֖ן עַל הָאָבְנָ֑יִם אִם בֵּ֥ן הוּא֙ וַהֲמִתֶּ֣ן אֹת֔וֹ וְאִם בַּ֥ת הִ֖יא וָחָֽיָה

verses.restored: But the midwives feared/revered the Divine, and they did not do as king of Egypt spoke to them; they let the boys live.

familiar.text: But the midwives feared God, and did not as the king of Egypt commanded them, but saved the men children alive.

modern.text: The midwives, however, feared God and did not do as the king of Egypt had instructed; they let the boys live.

original.text: וַתִּירֶ֤אןָ הַֽמְיַלְּדֹת֙ אֶת הָ֣אֱלֹהִ֔ים וְלֹ֣א עָשׂ֔וּ כַּאֲשֶׁ֛ר דִּבֶּ֥ר אֲלֵיהֶ֖ן מֶ֣לֶךְ מִצְרָ֑יִם וַתְּחַיֶּ֖יןָ אֶת הַיְלָדִֽים

verses.restored: The king of Egypt called the midwives and said to them, Why have you done this thing and let the boys live?

familiar.text: And the king of Egypt called for the midwives, and said unto them, Why have ye done this thing, and have saved the men children alive?

modern.text: So the king of Egypt summoned the midwives and asked them, “Why have you done this? Why have you let the boys live?”

original.text: וַיִּקְרָ֤א מֶֽלֶךְ מִצְרַ֨יִם֙ לַֽמְיַלְּדֹ֔ת וַיֹּ֣אמֶר לָהֶ֔ן מַדּ֥וּעַ עֲשִׂיתֶ֖ן הַדָּבָ֣ר הַזֶּ֑ה וַתְּחַיֶּ֖יןָ אֶת הַיְלָדִֽים

verses.restored: The midwives said to Pharaoh, Because the Hebrew women are not like the Egyptian women; for they are vigorous/life-filled, and before the midwife comes to them, they have given birth.

familiar.text: And the midwives said unto Pharaoh, Because the Hebrew women are not as the Egyptian women; for they are lively, and are delivered ere the midwives come in unto them.

modern.text: The midwives answered Pharaoh, “The Hebrew women are not like the Egyptian women, for they are vigorous and give birth before a midwife arrives.”

original.text: וַתֹּאמַ֤רְןָ הַֽמְיַלְּדֹת֙ אֶל פַּרְעֹ֔ה כִּ֣י לֹ֧א כַנָּשִׁ֛ים הַמִּצְרִיֹּ֖ת הָֽעִבְרִיֹּ֑ת כִּֽי חָי֣וֹת הֵ֔נָּה בְּטֶ֨רֶם תָּב֧וֹא אֲלֵהֶ֛ן הַמְיַלֶּ֖דֶת וְיָלָֽדוּ

verses.restored: And the Divine did good to the midwives, and the people multiplied and became very mighty.

familiar.text: Therefore God dealt well with the midwives: and the people multiplied, and waxed very mighty.

modern.text: So God was good to the midwives, and the people multiplied and became even more numerous.

original.text: וַיֵּ֥יטֶב אֱלֹהִ֖ים לַֽמְיַלְּדֹ֑ת וַיִּ֧רֶב הָעָ֛ם וַיַּֽעַצְמ֖וּ מְאֹֽד

verses.restored: And because the midwives feared/revered the Divine, he made houses/households for them.

familiar.text: And it came to pass, because the midwives feared God, that he made them houses.

modern.text: And because the midwives feared God, He gave them families of their own.

original.text: וַיְהִ֕י כִּֽי יָֽרְא֥וּ הַֽמְיַלְּדֹ֖ת אֶת הָאֱלֹהִ֑ים וַיַּ֥עַשׂ לָהֶ֖ם בָּתִּֽים

verses.restored: Then Pharaoh commanded all his people, saying, Every son born, cast him into the Nile, but every daughter let live.

familiar.text: And Pharaoh charged all his people, saying, Every son that is born ye shall cast into the river, and every daughter ye shall save alive.

modern.text: Then Pharaoh commanded all his people: “Every son born to the Hebrews you must throw into the Nile, but every daughter you may allow to live.”

original.text: וַיְצַ֣ו פַּרְעֹ֔ה לְכָל עַמּ֖וֹ לֵאמֹ֑ר כָּל הַבֵּ֣ן הַיִּלּ֗וֹד הַיְאֹ֨רָה֙ תַּשְׁלִיכֻ֔הוּ וְכָל הַבַּ֖ת תְּחַיּֽוּן

translation_notes: Hebrew title Shemot means Names; Exodus opens with names against imperial erasure.
Multiplication language echoes Genesis creation blessing.
Avad/avodah service language is central: Egypt turns service into crushing bondage, while Exodus will move toward service/worship of YHWH.
Midwives Shiphrah and Puah are named resistance figures; their reverence for Divine overrides Pharaoh's death-command.
safety_note: The chapter critiques Pharaoh's imperial oppression, forced labor, and birth violence. Do not turn Egypt/Egyptians into an ethnic enemy; the target is oppressive state power and fear-based domination.
